This Writ Petition has been filed for issuance of a Writ of declaration, declaring the properties comprised in Old S.No.182 and presently comprised in T.S.No.12/12 to an extent of acre 0.49 cents (19.847 ares) of the first petitioner and T.S.No.12/13 to an extent of 78 cents (31.594 ares) of the second petitioner, totally to an extent of 1.27 acres, situated at Dharapuram Town, Dharapuram Taluk, Tirupur District, forming part of MAP No.2, DDP/R (S)
No.03/93 dated 12.05.1993 for Dharapuram Local Planning Area Detailed Development Plan No.9,
in virtue of Section 38 of the Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act, 1971.
2.

The case of the petitioners is that the properties in Old S.No.182 and presently comprised in T.S.No.12/12 to an extent of acre 0.49 cents (19.847 ares) of the first petitioner and T.S.No.12/13 to an extent of 78 cents (31.594 ares) of the second petitioner, situated at Dharapuram Town,
Dharapuram Taluk, Tirupur District, originally belong to the petitioners' predecessor.
While so, a proposal was established in the name of 'Detailed Development Plan' for Dharapuram Town.

The Government has notified the same through notification as Periyar District Gazette No.9 dated C.Varadharaj vs The Assistant Director on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162475317/
2 28.09.1992.

On such notification, the Government had notified/reserved the lands in Old https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis S.No.182 and presently comprised in T.S.No.12/12 to an extent of acre 0.49 cents (19.847 ares) of the first petitioner and T.S.No.12/13 to an extent of 78 cents (31.594 ares) of the second petitioner, situated at Dharapuram Town, Dharapuram Taluk, Tirupur District.

Once the Detailed Government Plan comes into operation, the Government has to acquire the land under Section 36 of the Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act and appropriate compensation has to be provided under Section 39 of the Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act, within the period of three years.

sentences.text: On the facts and circumstances of the present case, the petitioners have clearly stated in the affidavit, that even under the old Act VII of 1920, no steps were taken for the purpose of completing the acquisition within three years and the same has not been denied in the counter affidavit filed by the first respondent.

Even assuming that the said Scheme has been taken over under the Act 35 of 1972, even from the date of coming into effect of the Act within the period stipulated under Section 38, no steps have been taken by the respondents for acquiring the property for the purpose of open space stated to have been reserved under the North-East Extension Town Planning Scheme Part II, Aruppukottai sanctioned under G.O.Ms.No.474 LA dated 02.03.1969.
9.

Accordingly, this Writ Petition is allowed.

4. Following the same, this Court is of the view that the acquisition cannot be made at this stage,
since the period of three years as contemplated under the said provision is already over.

Accordingly, this Writ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Petition is allowed and the respondents are directed to release the land in Old S.No.182 and presently comprised in T.S.No.12/12 to an extent of acre 0.49 cents (19.847 ares) of the first petitioner and T.S.No.12/13 to an extent of 78 cents (31.594 ares) of the second petitioner, situated at Dharapuram Town, Dharapuram Taluk, Tirupur District (property), forming part of Dharapuram Local Planning Area Detailed Development Plan No.9, by virtue of Section 38 of the Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act, 1971, as expeditiously as C.Varadharaj vs The Assistant Director on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162475317/
